top10.introHtml: Refreshed 2026-07-31. Found ~158 total convertibles across Cars.com, CarGurus, and AutoTrader before filtering. After applying the 4-seat rule, personal exclude list, and deduplication: 42 unique listings remain. TrueCar body-style filter remains broken — statically zeroed. Listings outside 35 mi (Cars.com page 2 returns a few at 38–41 mi) are included since the sources returned them. No manual transmissions were confirmed this refresh — see Manual tab. Exclusions noted: Cadillac Allante (2-seat), Toyota Paseo (2-seat), Ford Thunderbird (2-seat roadster).

picks.whyGood: The CLK Cabriolet is the hidden gem of this search — a genuinely pretty 4-seat soft-top with a proven 3.5L V6, only 65K miles, and sitting literally 2 miles from Media. Mercedes-Benz build quality at this price is exceptional. The CLK was designed as a long-distance cruiser with a well-engineered soft top that holds up better than the E-Class of the same era.
picks.whatToVerify: Full soft-top cycle: lower fully, raise fully, check for hesitation or error codes. Check headliner and rear seat carpet for water stains (CLK top drains can clog). Inspect A-pillar felt seals. Oil seepage from cam cover gaskets is normal wear — ask for recent service records. Check timing chain rattle on cold start (bank 2 stretch on 272 engines).
picks.bottomLine: Two miles from home, low miles, elegant design — easiest daily-driver pick in the entire search.

picks.whyGood: A 2006 GT with only 42,969 miles is extraordinarily rare — most S197 GTs of this vintage have 100K+. The 4.6L 3-valve V8 sounds incredible with the top down, parts are cheap and plentiful, and the 8.8-inch rear axle is bulletproof. Tom Masano Ford is a reputable dealer. Worth the 40-mile drive.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 specifics: cam-phaser rattle on cold start (common on 05–08 3V 4.6L — listen carefully before oil warms). Check spring perch and subframe for rust. Operate convertible top through full cycle including latch mechanism. Check rear-seat water staining. Ask for service history on the cam phasers.
picks.bottomLine: Lowest-mileage V8 Mustang in the region — the drive to Shillington is worth it.

picks.whyGood: The A3 Cabriolet is Audi's most practical and reliable soft-top — modern safety features (MQB platform), a tight Webasto-sourced soft top with good drainage, and the 2.0T engine is well-sorted by 2016. Private seller often means real ownership history and honest disclosure. Clean title confirmed.
picks.whatToVerify: DSG service history (7-speed S-tronic fluid change due by 40K, check if done). Soft-top frame alignment — A3 tops can develop a gap at the B-pillar if not adjusted. Check rear plastic window clarity. Audi water ingress: check passenger footwell for dampness. Inspect DSG mechatronic unit for any fault codes.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern car in the top 10 with full connectivity and safety kit — great daily at this price.

picks.whyGood: The E88 128i is the BMW to buy in this price range — the N52 inline-6 is one of BMW's most reliable modern engines (no turbo to fail, VANOS rarely problematic), and 51K miles on a 2012 is genuinely low. West Chester is 9 miles away. The 128i is lighter and more tossable than the 3-series convertible.
picks.whatToVerify: Top hydraulic rams — cycle the roof fully, listen for pump strain or slow movement. Check oil level (N52 can consume). Inspect cooling system (plastic components age). Check for any VANOS fault codes. Soft-top seal along rear window seam. Confirm power top is on the correct adjustment and latches without forcing.
picks.bottomLine: Low-mile N52 1-series nearby — BMW reliability at its best in this platform generation.

picks.whyGood: The IS 250C is the most mechanically reliable convertible in this search — Lexus build quality, retractable hardtop that virtually never fails, and the 2.5L V6 is nearly bulletproof. Clean title from a private seller exchange means it's been pre-vetted. 91K on a Lexus is barely broken in.
picks.whatToVerify: Hardtop mechanism: run through at least 3 full cycles, listen for any motor strain or door-seal squeak. Check trunk seal weather-stripping. Rear-window defroster function. The IS 250C's trunk is tiny when the top is stowed — confirm it meets your needs. Inspect for any oil seepage around valve cover.
picks.bottomLine: The Lexus is the most reliability-forward pick — hardtop engineering beats soft-tops in longevity every time.

picks.whyGood: The 435i xDrive is the best performance bargain in this search — a turbocharged 302hp inline-6 all-wheel-drive convertible for $8,500 is remarkable. Clean title from private seller exchange. The N55 engine is more reliable than the earlier N54. xDrive means confidence in all weather.
picks.whatToVerify: High miles mean scrutinize: check for oil leaks (N55 valve cover, oil filter housing gasket). Inspect soft-top for tears and rear window seal. Test xDrive transfer case and differential seals. Run a full ISTA scan for fault codes. Budget $500-800 for a pre-purchase inspection at an independent BMW shop.
picks.bottomLine: Best dollar-per-horsepower in the search, but get a PPI at an indy BMW shop before buying.

picks.whyGood: The 428i xDrive is the sensible 4-series pick — the N20 2.0T is less thirsty than the 435i and still pulls well. Clean title, private seller exchange vetting, 16 miles away. xDrive adds confidence in the wet. Good deal rating suggests fair pricing for the mileage.
picks.whatToVerify: N20 timing chain — listen for any rattle on cold start (known weak point on early N20s; 2014 was improved but not immune). Check soft-top hydraulic rams (16-second cycle is normal; slower means low fluid). Inspect for water ingress in trunk and footwells. Check water pump (electric, can fail without warning).
picks.bottomLine: Practical everyday 4-series with AWD and clean title — solid second-car choice.

picks.whyGood: A 2012 Mustang at 9 miles away for under $10,500 is hard to argue with. The S197 platform is proven, parts are the cheapest of any car on this list, and the 3.7L V6 (if V6) makes 305hp — no longer the penalty box of old. West Chester makes this a convenient look.
picks.whatToVerify: Identify the engine first (V6 vs GT) from the VIN or door sticker. Operate the convertible top and check all latches. Check rear-seat water staining. Inspect the 8.8 rear axle for clunk on take-off. Look at subframe and spring perches for any rust. Ask about top replacement history.
picks.bottomLine: Closest Mustang in the search — confirm V6 vs GT and check the top before buying.

picks.whyGood: The S550 Mustang Premium has modern amenities (IRS rear suspension, SYNC, backup camera) that the S197 lacks. Premium trim means heated seats and premium audio. Despite the miles, the 2.3 EcoBoost or 5.0 V8 (verify from VIN) in this generation is robust. Good value for a near-modern Mustang.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm engine from VIN (EcoBoost vs GT). S550: check MT-82 shifter feel if manual, IRS rear subframe bushings, rear camera function. Check convertible top operation and seals — S550 tops are more complex than S197. Look for any prior collision repairs. Ask dealer about warranty options.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang in the search — worth it if the engine and top check out.

picks.whyGood: Only 44,625 miles on a V8 E64 650i is exceptional — most have 150K by now. The N62 4.8L V8 is a magnificent engine when healthy. Private seller (Dale) often means careful ownership. At $13K, this is strong value for a grand-touring 6-series with the top down at 70mph.
picks.whatToVerify: N62 Vanos seals — this is the critical check; repair is $800-1500 and symptoms are rough cold idle. Check all 8 spark plugs (access through wheel wells — if neglected, budget $400). Power-top hydraulic system: all 4 latches must release and lock cleanly. Check SMG or 6-speed auto shift quality. Budget for the PPI.
picks.bottomLine: Lowest-mileage luxury convertible in the region — get a PPI, then enjoy the V8 soundtrack.

manual10.introHtml: No manual-transmission convertibles were confirmed in this refresh. All listings with transmission: null defaulted to null (unknown) — none were explicitly flagged as Manual by any source. Models in the search that may come in manual (2013 BMW 328i Convertible, 2012/2014 Ford Mustang) should be confirmed by calling the seller. The BMW E93 328i offered a 6-speed manual in the US through 2013; the Mustang V6 and GT both offered a 6-speed manual. Check VIN decoder or call the dealer to confirm before dismissing these.

mustangs.introHtml: Five 2005+ Ford Mustang convertibles found across all sources. Ranked GT > higher trim > lower miles > closer distance. The 2006 GT at 42,969 miles is the clear standout.

picks.whyGood: S197 GT with only 42,969 miles — extraordinary for a 2006. V8 sound, proven 4.6L 3-valve, parts everywhere. Sold by a Ford dealer. Standout in this price range.
picks.whatToVerify: Cam-phaser rattle cold, spring perch rust, top latch mechanism, rear-seat water staining, 8.8 axle clunk on take-off.
picks.bottomLine: The GT to buy — lowest miles, V8, reputable dealer.

picks.whyGood: S550 Premium brings IRS, modern safety tech, SYNC 3, and premium audio. Despite 141K miles, the EcoBoost or 5.0 V8 in this gen is durable. Best modern-platform Mustang in budget.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm engine (EcoBoost vs V8 from VIN), IRS rear subframe bushings, S550 convertible top seal quality, check for collision history.
picks.bottomLine: Best technology in the Mustang lineup — verify the engine and top before buying.

picks.whyGood: 9 miles away, under $10,500, mid-cycle S197 with refined suspension tune vs early cars. If V6, it makes 305hp — respectable. Good proximity for easy inspection.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm trim/engine, top operation and latch sealing, rear spring perch rust, 8.8 axle.
picks.bottomLine: Closest Mustang — confirm the engine trim and go look at it this weekend.

picks.whyGood: Budget Mustang entry point at $9,995 — the 2014 V6 is the last S197 generation with a smooth 305hp engine. Clean title, no accidents. High miles but Mustang V6 drivetrains are simple and proven.
picks.whatToVerify: High miles: check transmission fluid condition, top latch function, rear-seat water staining, spring perch rust inspection underneath.
picks.bottomLine: Cheapest entry into a clean S197 Mustang — budget option with high miles.

picks.whyGood: Same-year Mustang from a Ford dealer — Keyser Miller Ford adds dealer reconditioning and warranty options. Price is $490 more than the Cars.com listing but comes with dealer peace of mind.
picks.whatToVerify: Same as rank 4. Ask about any dealer reconditioning work done. Confirm trim from sticker. Request CarFax if not already provided.
picks.bottomLine: Dealer-backed Mustang at nearly identical price to rank 4 — choose based on which seller gives more confidence.
